question: Find the acute angle between the planes $2x-y+2z=3$ and $x+2y-2z=5$.
explanation:
Step 1: Normal vectors of the planes
The direction ratios of the normals to the planes are obtained from their coefficients. Thus,
$$\vec{n}_1=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k},\quad \vec{n}_2=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}.$$
Step 2: Angle-between-planes relation
The acute angle $\theta$ between two planes is the acute angle between their normal vectors. Therefore,
$$\cos\theta=\frac{|\vec{n}_1\cdot\vec{n}_2|}{|\vec{n}_1||\vec{n}_2|}.$$
Step 3: Scalar product
$$\vec{n}_1\cdot\vec{n}_2=2(1)+(-1)(2)+2(-2)=-4.$$
Step 4: Magnitudes and simplification
$$|\vec{n}_1|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3,\quad |\vec{n}_2|=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3.$$
Hence,
$$\cos\theta=\frac{|-4|}{3\times3}=\frac{4}{9}.$$
Step 5: Final result
Therefore, the acute angle between the planes is
$$\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right).$$
